title: Making weekend plans
scenario: Two friends are making plans for the weekend. Listen for the day, the final time and the meeting place.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.german: Ja, am Nachmittag. Wollen wir im Park spazieren gehen?
lines.english: Yes, in the afternoon. Shall we go for a walk in the park?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.german: Gern. Treffen wir uns um halb drei?
lines.english: Gladly. Shall we meet at half past two?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.german: Lieber um drei. Ich esse vorher noch zu Mittag.
lines.english: I'd prefer three. I'm having lunch before that.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.german: Gut, dann um drei am Eingang zum Park.
lines.english: Good, then at three at the entrance to the park.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.english: It's a plan! See you on Sunday.

questions.explanation: They say ‘am Sonntag’ — on Sunday — and confirm it with ‘Bis Sonntag’.

questions.prompt: What time do they finally agree on?
questions.explanation: ‘Halb drei’ means 2:30, but Sam suggests ‘lieber um drei’. Alex agrees: ‘dann um drei’ — so the final time is 3:00 pm.
‘Am Eingang zum Park’ means at the entrance to the park.

questions.prompt: What are they planning to do?
questions.explanation: ‘Im Park spazieren gehen’ means to go for a walk in the park. Sam will eat lunch beforehand.

practice.tip: In ‘Zeit’, z starts with /ts/, like the end of English ‘cats’. Let your voice rise gently at the end of this yes/no question.
German w in ‘wir’ sounds like English v. In ‘treffen’, keep the e short, as in English ‘bed’. ‘Halb drei’ means half an hour before three: 2:30.
practice.rhythm: GERN. TREFFen wir uns um halb DREI?

practice.tip: In ‘Eingang’, ei sounds like English ‘eye’. The ng is one sound, as at the end of ‘sing’; do not add a separate hard g. Give the time and place a little extra emphasis.
practice.rhythm: Gut, dann um DREI / am EINgang zum PARK.
